requirement: The review prompt MUST direct the reviewer never to rename or move a committed requirement, and to raise a wrong name as a design question instead. When the reviewer splits a committed requirement, the prompt MUST direct it to keep the requirement's full name on the core obligation, to name the parts `<name>.<part>`, and to list every new name.
rationale:
The requirement has four obligations on the review prompt:
- Never rename or move a committed requirement.
- Raise a wrong name as a design question.
- When splitting, keep the full name on the core obligation and name the parts `<name>.<part>`.
- List every new name.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_review_prompt_never_renames_and_names_split_parts]` covers all four. It uses `review_prompt_between` to take the bundled `habeas-requirements/references/review-prompt.md` text between `**Mechanical changes:**` and `**Design questions:**`. `collapse` joins whitespace, so line wrapping does not matter. `assert_text` then asserts that this section contains each of three phrases:
- "Never rename or move a committed requirement; if its name is wrong, raise it as a design question" covers the first two obligations.
- "When you split one, keep its full name on the core obligation and name the parts `<name>.<part>`" covers the third.
- "List every new name" covers the fourth.

The assertions are real `contains` checks that panic on a miss. The test also scopes them to the mechanical-changes section, where the instruction applies. The prompt text in the asset contains exactly these sentences. The requirement concerns prompt content, so a phrase-presence test is the appropriate check. No obligation or boundary is left untested.
